title: Canary- and Rollback-Aware Composite Scoring for Predicting Operational Risk of Agentic NetOps Actions: An Artifact‑Backed Null and Reproducibility Report
abstract: We preregistered and executed a fully hashed paired confirmatory study (CNSM2026-04-canary-rollback-metrics-v1) to evaluate whether a composite operational‑risk score (verifier_coverage, canary_sim_pass, rollback_success_prob, LLM_confidence, abstention_utility) discriminates emulator-measured outages better than the best single submetric. Using a deterministic synthetic NetOps task bank and a deterministic validator we executed 200 held‑out paired tasks (baseline vs guarded) and preserved exhaustive execution artifacts (responses, per‑episode scoring JSONs with validator traces, provider‑call traces, execution manifest, analysis CSVs). Persisted traces show baseline_success_count = 200/200 and guarded_success_count = 200/200 (n11=200,n10=0,n01=0,n00=0). Paired-bootstrap 95% CI for the paired difference = [0.0, 0.0] (bootstrap_seed=1729, resamples=10000); McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. The preregistered AUC‑ROC primary estimand is undefined for this held‑out set because labels are constant. Two preregistered artifacts required to recompute the AUC comparison (consolidated per‑episode submetrics CSV and serialized trained composite model weights) are not present in the preserved bundle; we document exact persisted artifact paths and SHA‑256 hashes, provide a deterministic reconstruction recipe using only preserved artifacts, and give an artifact‑hygiene checklist for future discriminative validations.

sections.introduction: Agentic LLMs for NetOps can convert operator intent into device configuration rapidly, but operationalizing such proposals requires rigorous assurance: validators, canary trials, rollback testing, and abstention policies are common mitigations. We preregistered CNSM2026-04-canary-rollback-metrics-v1 to ask: does a composite canary–rollback score (verifier_coverage, canary_sim_pass, rollback_success_prob, LLM_confidence, abstention_utility) predict emulator‑measured outage (binary) better than any single submetric? The study design, split seeds, analysis recipe, and persistence expectations were frozen prior to execution (preregistration SHA‑256 = 553509f5d61a7f0df674b676b1091ccbe734c2d142b52e65d81932fae8657cee). We executed a deterministic paired baseline vs guarded run on N=200 held‑out pairs using declared model gpt‑5‑mini (see execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa) and a deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). This paper reports artifact‑grounded outcomes, documents why the preregistered discriminative AUC estimand cannot be recomputed from the preserved bundle, and provides a deterministic reconstruction recipe and concrete fixes.
sections.related_work: Operational NetOps work increasingly emphasizes generate–verify–repair patterns, verifier interposition, and canary/rollback instrumentation as essential to safe automation. Prior work motivates per‑proposal verification and cost‑aware verification orchestration (e.g., MeshAgent-style constraint grounding, GVR architectures, SEVER-style verifier orchestration). Our contribution is methodological and reproducibility‑oriented: a preregistered, fully hashed paired run with exhaustive validator traces that (a) demonstrates a deterministic ceiling outcome on the chosen synthetic bank and (b) locates explicit artifact omissions that prevent recomputation of a preregistered discriminative estimand.
sections.methodology: Preregistration summary. The preregistered study id is CNSM2026-04-canary-rollback-metrics-v1 (preregistration SHA‑256 reported above). Key frozen elements: model family (declared gpt‑5‑mini), deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), synthetic task bank generation and deterministic splits (train=300,val=100,test=200), paired baseline vs guarded condition, primary estimand (difference in AUC‑ROC: composite vs best single submetric), analysis recipe (L2 logistic regression with 5‑fold CV on train+val, DeLong test for AUC difference), bootstrap CI (seed=1729, 10000 resamples), max_model_calls=400, and exact artifacts required to be persisted (per‑episode scoring JSONs, consolidated_submetrics.csv, composite_model_weights.pkl). Execution contract and deterministic generation. The run used a shared_initial_candidate policy so each pair used the same initial generation across conditions. The execution manifest records planned_episode_count=400 and completed_episode_count=400 (execution/execution_manifest.json; full hash manifest included in evidence bundle). Artifact persistence and hashing policy. We persisted raw model outputs (execution/responses/*.txt), per‑episode scoring JSONs with validator_trace fields (execution/scoring/*.json), provider call traces (execution/provider_calls/*.json), the execution manifest, and analysis CSVs (analysis/*.csv). Representative persisted paths and SHA‑256 hashes are cited below and in the Disclosure. Predefined submetrics and extraction fields (preregistered). The preregistration defined submetrics and required persisted fields: verifier_coverage = validator_trace.validation_after.observed_touched_field_count / validator_trace.validation_after.required_command_count; canary_sim_pass = per‑episode canary simulation pass flag (expected in provider_calls or scoring JSONs); rollback_success_prob = persisted rollback trial success or derived from provider call traces; LLM_confidence = model confidence numeric field (expected in provider_calls); abstention_utility = persisted utility proxy for abstention decisions. The preregistration required a consolidated_submetrics.csv (one row per episode with the five submetrics) and composite_model_weights.pkl (serialized training artifact) to be persisted for reproducible evaluation.
sections.results: Artifact‑grounded facts. Execution counts and manifest: planned_episode_count = 400, completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0, model_calls_used = 200 (execution/execution_manifest.json; manifest and full hash manifest included). Held‑out test outcomes (extracted from persisted execution/scoring/*.json): baseline_success_count = 200/200 and guarded_success_count = 200/200. The persisted paired contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; SHA‑256 = 7bc1bd2a42b5ac3f7adb61db47cf8dbe0472f678032abcd1e7c44f92ea2de71c) records n11=200, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0. Confirmatory statistics computed from persisted contingency table: paired success‑rate difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; paired‑bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (bootstrap_seed=1729, resamples=10000; artifact analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA‑256 = c56b737a55780f99fe36a9650ee69f18694a666348d4643c0dd8240e1757406d). Primary AUC estimand status. Because the held‑out label vector is constant (no positive outage labels among test N=200), AUC‑ROC and AUPRC comparisons are undefined; therefore the preregistered primary discriminative estimand (AUC difference between composite and best submetric) cannot be computed from the preserved bundle. Missing preregistered persisted artifacts. The preregistration required two additional persisted artifacts that are absent from the evidence bundle: (a) consolidated_submetrics.csv (row per episode with verifier_coverage, canary_sim_pass, rollback_success_prob, LLM_confidence, abstention_utility) and (b) composite_model_weights.pkl (serialized trained L2 logistic regression weights plus feature normalization parameters). Their absence prevents recomputing the composite model and its discriminative AUC on the held‑out test set from the supplied artifacts alone. Per‑preregistered‑submetric availability (artifact‑grounded). From the preserved execution/scoring and provider_calls JSONs we determined the following availability (exact field pointers follow): - verifier_coverage: PRESENT. Extract from execution/scoring/<episode>.json → validator_trace.validation_after.observed_touched_field_count and validator_trace.validation_after.required_command_count (representative file: execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json; SHA‑256 = 90844c2baf63d1a1eb8ed5d6b26bfb38a7941ec4c4f1af9cb8930a33e9cc4478). - canary_sim_pass: ABSENT. No canary_sim_result or equivalent boolean field found in execution/provider_calls/*.json or execution/scoring/*.json in the preserved bundle. - rollback_success_prob: ABSENT. No rollback_trial_result or rollback_success field is present in provider_call traces. - LLM_confidence: ABSENT. execution/provider_calls/*.json and response files do not include a numeric confidence field per episode. - abstention_utility: ABSENT. No persisted abstain_decision or abstention_utility is present. Deterministic reconstruction recipe (artifact‑only, no new model calls). Using preserved artifacts one can reproducibly: 1) recompute per‑episode binary labels by reading execution/scoring/<episode>.json → validator_trace.validation_after.valid (examples provided under execution/scoring/*.json); 2) compute verifier_coverage = observed_touched_field_count / required_command_count for episodes (fields present in scoring JSONs); 3) reproduce the paired contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv is already persisted); 4) reproduce McNemar and the bootstrap CI reported (analysis/*.csv and analysis/analysis_log.jsonl are present). To obtain the missing submetrics (canary_sim_pass, rollback_success_prob, LLM_confidence, abstention_utility) without re‑running LLMs one must deterministically replay or emulate the canary/rollback simulators used at execution time using the original simulator code and seeds (these simulators were not persisted as consolidated CSV in the bundle). Representative persisted examples. Representative per‑episode scoring JSON: execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (SHA‑256 = 90844c2baf63d1a1eb8ed5d6b26bfb38a7941ec4c4f1af9cb8930a33e9cc4478) contains validator_trace.validation_after (final_state, normalized_configuration, observed_touched_field_count, required_command_count, valid=true). Representative execution manifest/config: execution/model_configuration.json (SHA‑256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa); execution/execution_manifest.json (full hash manifest referenced in evidence bundle). All preserved artifact paths and a full hash manifest are included in the evidence bundle.
sections.discussion: Interpretation. The preserved evidence shows a deterministic ceiling: the deterministic validator accepted every candidate configuration in both baseline and guarded conditions on the chosen synthetic bank leading to constant test labels and hence an undefined AUC comparison. This is a scientifically meaningful null/ceiling outcome: with the given synthetic bank, validator predicates, and shared_initial generation policy, the test partition contained no emulator‑measured outages, so discriminative evaluation of composite risk scores on this holdout is impossible. Reproducibility diagnosis and remediation. The artifact bundle contains all raw generation outputs, per‑episode scoring JSONs with validator traces, provider call traces, execution manifest, and analysis CSVs sufficient to verify the paired contingency claim and to reproduce the McNemar/bootstrap inference. The specific missing persisted artifacts (consolidated_submetrics.csv and composite_model_weights.pkl) are deterministic and remediable: persist these files at runtime (with exact canonical column names and normalization parameters) or deterministically derive the missing submetrics by replaying recorded deterministic canary/rollback simulators on the preserved provider_call traces and scoring JSONs. Practical artifact‑hygiene checklist (required filenames and fields). For future runs we recommend persisting at runtime with exact filenames and fields: - consolidated_submetrics.csv — columns: episode_id,pair_id,verifier_coverage,canary_sim_pass,rollback_success_prob,LLM_confidence,abstention_utility. - composite_model_weights.pkl — serialized L2 weights + feature normalization params + training RNG seed. - retrain_script.py — deterministic dependencies file (requirements.txt) and RNG seed. - canary_simulator_log.json and rollback_trial_log.json — per‑episode deterministic simulator outputs with SHA‑256. Threats to validity. Internal: deterministic validator semantics and the shared_initial generation policy reduce variance but can induce ceiling effects. Construct: emulator outage labels may not equate to production outage risk. External: single declared model (gpt‑5‑mini) and synthetic tasks limit generalization. Conclusion validity: N=200 sufficient for paired tests but uninformative when labels are constant. Operational implications. Discriminative validation of composite risk metrics requires (a) test partitions containing nonzero prevalence of adverse outcomes (seeded faults, adversarial prompts, adversarially crafted topologies), and (b) rigorous artifact persistence (the checklist above) to enable exact recomputation of classifiers and AUCs.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a deterministic, artifact‑backed paired NetOps experiment. Persisted validator traces show every held‑out task validated correctly under both baseline and guarded conditions (n11=200), yielding a paired difference of 0.0 (95% bootstrap CI = [0.0,0.0]; McNemar p = 1.0). The preregistered AUC‑ROC comparison cannot be computed from the preserved bundle because (i) the held‑out labels are constant and (ii) two preregistered artifacts required for recomputation (consolidated_submetrics.csv and composite_model_weights.pkl) were not persisted. We supply exact artifact paths and SHA‑256 hashes for all preserved evidence, an artifact‑grounded submetric availability map, a deterministic reconstruction recipe, and a concrete artifact‑hygiene checklist. The scientific contribution is methodological: an exemplar of preregistration, deterministic artifact persistence, and an explicit, verifiable reproducibility diagnosis that identifies the precise artifact omissions to fix before attempting discriminative composite‑score validation in agentic NetOps settings.

disclosure_statement: Autonomy, pre-lock human role, and immutable initial master prompt. A human Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI / LLMs for NetOps) and approved the autonomy boundary prior to the autonomy lock. After the lock, all literature review, preregistration, experiment design freeze, code generation, experiment execution, artifact hashing, analysis, and manuscript drafting reported here were performed autonomously without manual human editing of technical content. Declared LLM and configuration. Declared model: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA-256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). Adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Immutable initial master prompt. The immutable initial master prompt used by the autonomous researcher is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba) and was not modified after the autonomy lock. Preregistration. The preregistered study id is CNSM2026-04-canary-rollback-metrics-v1; the preregistration JSON SHA-256 is 553509f5d61a7f0df674b676b1091ccbe734c2d142b52e65d81932fae8657cee (recorded in the execution manifest). Evidence retention and omission. The evidence bundle contains per-episode raw responses (execution/responses/*.txt), per-episode scoring JSONs (execution/scoring/*.json — representative example execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json SHA-256 = 90844c2baf63d1a1eb8ed5d6b26bfb38a7941ec4c4f1af9cb8930a33e9cc4478), provider-call traces (execution/provider_calls/*.json), the execution manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json), and analysis CSVs (analysis/*.csv) with recorded SHA-256 hashes (representative hashes cited in the manuscript). The preregistered artifacts that were NOT persisted into the evidence bundle are (a) the consolidated per-episode submetric summary CSV (consolidated_submetrics.csv) and (b) the serialized trained-composite-model weights file (composite_model_weights.pkl). Because those two artifacts were not persisted, the preregistered AUC-ROC composite-vs-best-submetric comparison cannot be recomputed from the supplied bundle without deterministic reconstruction or re-running canary/rollback simulations (which would create new derived artifacts). Safety and operational scope. Experiments used synthetic tasks and containerized emulators only; no production devices or proprietary vendor images were used. No technical restarts affected scientific outcomes (execution manifest: failed_episode_count=0). All retained artifacts are hashed and listed in the execution manifest; representative hashes are cited above and in the manuscript.
limitations: Synthetic task bank and deterministic emulator: tasks and validator may not capture real-world nondeterminism, device heterogeneity, or latent failure modes.
Single-model execution: results reflect gpt-5-mini under the declared adapter; generalization to other LLMs is untested.
Ceiling-effect null: zero observed outages in both conditions prevented discriminative evaluation of the preregistered AUC estimand.
Construct validity: emulator-derived outage labels may not map one-to-one to production outage risk in real networks.

Artifact omission: serialized trained-composite-model weights and a consolidated per-episode submetric summary CSV were not persisted to the evidence bundle (documented execution artifact-collection omission).
